newsitem.title: LATVIA: REUTERS BALTIC NEWS - MARKETS WHILE YOU SLEPT.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS BALTIC NEWS - MARKETS WHILE YOU SLEPT.

text.p: These are the main developments on markets overnight:

NEW-YORK. U.S. stocks finished higher as their record run continues in wake of Friday's U.S. jobs report. Dow rose by 43 points to 7478, its second straight record. Dow gains now stand at more than 1,000 points since start of 1997. Bonds weakened, meanwhile.
TOKYO. Stocks maintained their gains in early afternoon trade on Tuesday, supported by futures-linked buying as the yen/dollar rate stabilised.
LONDON. UK shares ended close day's highs, supported by Dow, strong FTSE futures and UK bank sector. Market shrugged off weak T-bills, sharp drop in European bourses.
FTSE finished at 4,686.7, rising by 41.7 points.
The dollar was steady by Tokyo noon due to buy-back interst by overseas speculative funds and public and private institutional investors.
The U.S. unit stood 112.86/89 against the yen at 0300 GMT.
The dollar's recovery against the yen from early lows was helped by a large pound buying for the yen by a major local brokerage firm.
